text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Doubts about the future of the Lithuanian currency will increase instability in the Baltics, Estonian financial experts say.
- Coalition Party parliament faction head Mart Siimann admits in an interview that Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi has made mistakes but is not convinced Vaehi should resign.
- The language department plans to test the allegedly insufficient knowledge of Estonian language of the Maardu and Sillamae council members in northeast Estonia.
- Nine police constables in Eastern-Viru county who did not apply for Estonian citizenship have been dismissed under the public service law.
- The Estonian Embassy in Riga hopes to open a renovated building by February 24, Independence Day.
- A $10 million deal between the North-Estonian bank and a Swiss firm was initiated by the Bank of Estonia. The newspaper publishes copies of a secret agreement by the central bank, signed in 1993.
- The Council of Europe urges Estonia to pay more attention to teaching the Estonian language to its Russian population, mambers of Riigikogu CEPA delegation said at a press conference.
- Estonian legislation on money-laundering is expected to be drafted by this autumn, justice ministry officals said at an Estonian-EU joint seminar on the matter.
- The Development Paryty does not intend to back a vote of no-confidence against Vaehi, a member of the party's council Tiit Made said.
- Opposition parties may hold express a vote of no-confidence against Vaehi on February 10, the leading opposition party, the Reform Party, said.
